sentence: This project builds computer methods that use several sequencing technologies to put together genome assemblies for each haplotype.
This project studies how cell death and reactive chemicals in early brain injury cause motor problems in rabbits with a cerebral palsy model.
This project tries to find out which natural products let bacteria sense and respond to competition and alliance with other microbes.
This project builds a flexible carbon fiber array with penetrating electrodes for recording and stimulating nerve and brain activity.
This project tests how feedback from higher cortical areas changes the way the auditory cortex responds while animals listen and make decisions about sounds.
This project builds and tests a way to guide liver ablation as it happens by combining two imaging methods.
This project uses a mouse model to find out how changes in a signaling pathway affect the onset and growth of lung squamous cell cancer.
This project trains graduate scientists to work where chemistry and biology meet.
This project develops imaging methods, from making radiochemicals to forming images and estimating amounts from them.
This project offers high throughput screening of small and large molecules to help cancer researchers find drug targets and test drugs.
This project studies how phosphorylation and natural variation in G protein sequence change how heterotrimeric G proteins work and send signals.
This project studies how antimicrobials are used in dogs, cats, and horses to help fight antimicrobial resistance.
This project builds and tests pig models of glioblastoma to try out treatments before they are used in people.
This project builds a way to measure respectful and disrespectful language in medical records and tries to increase respect in healthcare.
This project studies how mutations in a calcium channel change nerve cell activity and calcium signaling in neurodevelopmental disorders.
This project tries to find out how a protein found in the brain changes the function and expression of a nicotinic receptor.
This project offers postdoctoral training in health sciences innovation for researchers in medicine, nursing, pharmacy and public health.
This project tries to find out how senescent cells develop, how they damage normal tissues, and how to kill them.
This project brings chemists, biochemists, engineers and bioinformaticians together to study how cells communicate along biological pathways in disease.
This project tries to find out how changes in translation control cause bone marrow failure and looks for small molecules to treat it.
